cohorts.subjects: Living adult patients whose lumbosacral MRI scans, made January 2007 to July 2012, were selected from all adults referred for lumbosacral MRI to the Department of Radiology, Fondazione di Ricerca e Cura 'Giovanni Paolo II', Universita Cattolica del Sacro Cuore, Campobasso, Italy; the abstract calls them prospectively enrolled, the methods selected. All from Central and Southern Italy and printed as of the same Caucasian race; called nonsymptomatic and free of known diseases. Excluded (Table 1): age under 20 or over 45; neurogenic claudication; severe, constant lumbosacral pain radiating to the legs; congenital diseases; oncological or haematological disease; previous spinal surgery or trauma; a lumbosacral transitional vertebra or other spinal abnormality on MRI; vertebral body scalloping; degenerative arthrosis on MRI; inflammatory, immunological or connective tissue disorders; chronic drug therapy; early menopause with osteopenia risk; any qualitative suspicion of stenosis or dural ectasia on the sagittal T1 and T2 images. Numbers screened and excluded not given. Weight and height were recorded but not reported.

techniques.instrument: GE Signa Excite HD 1.5 T; sagittal T1-weighted (TR/TE 420/8 ms) and T2-weighted (2700/102 ms) fast spin echo; slice 4 mm, spacing 0.4 mm, matrix 384 x 224, field of view 320 x 320 mm, 4 excitations; the measuring tool is not named (Inference: on-screen electronic calipers, the figures print values to 0.01 mm with decimal commas)
techniques.how: On sagittal images, at each level L1 to S1 at the vertebral body, not the disc: SCD perpendicular to the canal's long axis from the middle third of the posterior body wall to the front edge of the lamina at the base of the spinous process; DSD, the AP width of the dural sac, along the same line; VBD, the AP width of the body (soma) at the same height. DSR = DSD / VBD per level, and the ratio of S1 DSD to L4 DSD. T1 and T2 were read together to separate the anterior epidural fat from the ventral sac surface; at S1 the lines follow the sacral inclination (Figure 2). Normal limits are mean +/- 1.96 SD per sex and level (called a 95% CI). How levels were counted is not stated.
